subject: Chemistry
notes: Chemistry differs from Maths: NDA Chemistry is BASIC general-science (Class 9-10 level, small weight), while MHT-CET Chemistry is full +2 depth. So the spine follows BOARD ORDER with CET as the primary exam weight and NDA as a light overlay - NOT NDA-first (which would front-load basic general chemistry).
16 board chapters in board order, grouped into 5 teaching phases (physical -> atomic/bonding -> inorganic -> states/surface/equilibrium -> organic).
NCERT-11 (rationalised) dropped much of board XI: States of Matter, Hydrogen + s-Block, p-Block, Surface Chemistry, Nuclear Chemistry, Chemistry in Everyday Life are NCERT gaps.
Chapters with little/no CET weight (Analytical Chemistry, Analytical Techniques, Nuclear Chemistry, Chemistry in Everyday Life) are board-syllabus items kept for completeness.

CBSE/NCERT cohort gap: six chapters here — Elements of Group 1 & 2 (s-block), Elements of Group 13-15 (p-block), States of Matter, Adsorption & Colloids, Nuclear Chemistry, and Chemistry in Everyday Life — were removed from the rationalised NCERT syllabus, so CBSE students have NOT seen them. MHT-CET/JEE/NEET still test the physical/inorganic ones, so treat these as NEW content (not revision) for a CBSE cohort and cover them fully. Marked '⚠ CBSE gap'.

Two topics a CBSE cohort needs in Class 11 are taught by the State Board in XII: Chemical Thermodynamics and Ionic Equilibrium (the acid-base / pH / buffer / Ksp half of NCERT's single 'Equilibrium' chapter). For CBSE students, pull these forward from the XII plan before their Class 11 board exam — they are marked '◆ CBSE: teach in XI' there. (Analytical Chemistry & Analytical Techniques are NOT a gap: that content is retained in NCERT Ch.1 and Ch.8, only repackaged as standalone State-Board chapters.)

guiding_principles.meaning: XI Chemistry is driven by the board syllabus and MHT-CET (the +2 exam). Units follow board order; CET PYQ frequency is the primary weight.

NDA Chemistry tests only foundational/general chemistry (atomic structure basics, periodic trends, redox basics, organic/hydrocarbon basics, everyday-life chemistry). The NDA column flags which chapters carry that basic relevance; most +2 subtopics read 'NDA: none'.
Board order is grouped into physical/general -> atomic & bonding -> inorganic -> states/surface/equilibrium -> organic, following the board sequence without reordering.

phases.name: Foundations & Analytical Chemistry
phases.blurb: Mole concept, measurement, analytical methods - the quantitative base for everything else.

phases.name: Atomic Structure, Bonding & Redox
phases.blurb: Structure of the atom, chemical bonding, redox, and the periodic table - the theoretical core.

phases.name: States, Surface Chemistry & Equilibrium
phases.blurb: Gaseous state, adsorption & colloids, chemical equilibrium, and nuclear chemistry.

phases.name: Organic Chemistry
phases.blurb: Basic principles, hydrocarbons, and everyday-life chemistry - the organic foundation for XII.

units.title: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry
units.why_here: Mole concept, stoichiometry, laws of chemical combination - the quantitative language of all chemistry. High CET weight (Mole 40).

units.title: Introduction to Analytical Chemistry
units.why_here: Analytical methods, significant figures, empirical/molecular formula, stoichiometric calculations. Board-specific; low CET.

units.title: Some Analytical Techniques
units.why_here: Purification techniques (crystallization, distillation, chromatography, solvent extraction). Board-specific; supports organic chemistry.

units.title: Structure of Atom
units.why_here: Subatomic particles, atomic models, hydrogen spectrum, Bohr and quantum-mechanical model, quantum numbers, configuration. Core CET chapter.

units.title: Chemical Bonding
units.why_here: Ionic/covalent bonding, Lewis structures, VSEPR, valence-bond & molecular-orbital theory, hybridization, polarity. Core CET chapter.

units.title: Redox Reactions
units.why_here: Oxidation number, balancing redox, electrode potential. High CET weight (Oxidation Number 26).

units.title: Modern Periodic Table
units.why_here: Modern periodic table, blockwise characteristics, periodic trends. Foundational; also the main NDA-relevant chapter (periodic trends).

units.title: Elements of Group 1 and 2 (incl. Hydrogen)
units.why_here: Hydrogen + alkali & alkaline-earth metals: properties, reactions, important compounds. NCERT-11 dropped this (gap).

units.title: Elements of Group 13, 14 and 15
units.why_here: p-block Groups 13-15: trends, oxidation states, allotropy (incl. carbon allotropes - the main NDA link). Low CET; NCERT-11 dropped p-block.

units.title: States of Matter
units.why_here: Intermolecular forces, gas laws, ideal-gas equation. CET tests the gas-law content (bundled under Some Basic Concepts); NCERT-11 dropped States of Matter.

units.title: Adsorption and Colloids
units.why_here: Adsorption, physisorption/chemisorption, isotherms, colloids, catalysis. Maps to CET Surface Chemistry; NCERT-11 has no Surface Chemistry.

units.title: Chemical Equilibrium
units.why_here: Reversible reactions, law of mass action, Kc/Kp, Le Chatelier. NCERT Ch6 Equilibrium; the ionic-equilibrium depth is XII.

units.title: Nuclear Chemistry and Radioactivity
units.why_here: Nuclear stability, radioactivity, decay kinetics, binding energy. Board-specific; not in CET or NCERT-11.

units.title: Basic Principles of Organic Chemistry
units.why_here: Structural representation, classification, IUPAC nomenclature, electronic effects, isomerism, reaction intermediates. Core CET organic base.

units.title: Hydrocarbons
units.why_here: Alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, aromatic compounds - preparation, properties, reactions. Split across four CET chapters.

units.title: Chemistry in Everyday Life
units.why_here: Food chemistry, medicines, cleansing agents. Board/NDA everyday-life chemistry; low CET.
